title.narrative: Integrated Child Protection and Gender-Based Violence Response for Drought-Affected Communities in Xudur District, Bakool Region

description.narrative: ltpgtDignity First Somalia (DFS) proposes a six-month integrated but clearly delineated Child Protection (CP) and Gender-Based Violence (GBV) response to address escalating protection risks among severely drought-affected and displaced women, men, girls, and boys in Xudur District, Bakool Region. Recurrent drought, displacement, food insecurity, and weakened community coping mechanisms have significantly increased exposure to violence, exploitation, abuse, neglect, family separation, and harmful coping strategies—with women and girls facing heightened risks of GBV, and girls and boys experiencing increased child protection and psychosocial risks.ltbrgtThe project will directly reach 7,600 crisis-affected people, disaggregated as 3,280 women, 560 men, 2,960 girls, and 800 boys. Of these, 4,400 people (2,610 women, 240 men, 1,350 girls, and 200 boys) will be reached through GBV interventions, while 3,200 people (1,680 girls, 720 boys, 480 women, and 320 men) will be reached through Child Protection interventions. The majority of beneficiaries are internally displaced persons (6,020), with the remaining 1,580 drawn from drought-affected host communities.ltbrgtltbrgtGBV programming focuses on prevention, risk mitigation, and survivor-centred response. Women and girls, including GBV survivors and those at heightened risk, will access quality GBV case management, confidential referrals to health services including Clinical Management of Rape (CMR), psychosocial support, and dignity kits. The project will provide protection-linked cash assistance to 250 GBV survivors, delivered through case management to mitigate immediate safety risks and enable safe access to essential services. In parallel, men and boys will be engaged through mobile outreach and community awareness activities to disseminate GBV prevention messages, referral pathways, and PSEA information, contributing to safer and more accountable community environments.ltbrgtltbrgtMobile CP teams will conduct regular outreach in hard-to-reach locations and will be strategically deployed at nutrition and maternal and child health (MCH) service points to strengthen CP–Nutrition integration. At these sites, CP case workers will support early identification of at-risk girls and boys, provide child-focused MHPSS and Psychological First Aid (PFA), and facilitate timely referrals for child protection, GBV, health, and other essential services. This integrated approach enables early detection of protection risks among malnourished children and their caregivers, strengthens referral pathways, and ensures that children accessing nutrition services are linked to appropriate protection and psychosocial support, without duplicating nutrition service delivery.ltbrgtltbrgtLocalization, accountability, and inclusion underpin the project design. DFS will implementation through trained local staff and community-based structures, ensuring appropriate service delivery for women, men, girls, and boys. Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), PSEA, gender equality, and disability inclusion are integrated across all activities, supported by accessible Complaints and Feedback Mechanisms (CFM) and continuous community engagement. As part of risk mitigation and quality assurance, DFS will conduct routine safety audits of Child-Friendly Spaces, outreach locations, and service delivery points to ensure safety, dignity, and accessibility for all beneficiaries.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThrough close coordination with Protection, health and nutrition actors, and local authorities, the project complements other funded interventions and contributes to a coherent, principled, and life-saving protection response for women, men, girls, and boys.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtDFS will deliver services across 7 sites in Xudur (Hudur) District: Tuboy (4.14182, 43.84506), Shidle HN (4.123979, 43.878698), Daryeel FDP (4.114974, 43.88309), Gaabaney (4.122906, 43.91261), Madax Waraabe (4.12423, 43.91186), Waneey (4.21279, 43.98855), and Kontomo (4.124808, 43.857191), targeting 3,574 households.ltbrgtlt/pgt
